After having examined the submissions advanced by learnedcounsel for the parties and perused the FIR, we are of theopinion that considering the allegations levelled therein of chainsnatching of a lady for which she lodged the FIR under Section392 IPC, the investigation is underway and further for the otherprayers  made  in  the  writ  petition  by  the  petitioner,  nointerference is called for by this Court in its extraordinarypower under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

The petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
records.notes: Criminal writ petition under Article 226 seeking stay of arrest in Case Crime No. 83 of 2022 under Section 392 IPC (robbery / chain snatching). Division Bench examined allegations, noted investigation is underway, held no interference is called for in extraordinary powers under Article 226, and dismissed petition as lacking merit. State through Additional Government Advocate successfully opposed stay of arrest and defended the ongoing criminal investigation; successful party is state_prosecution under Section 5 Row 128.
records.case_title: /3065/2022 of JITENDRA PRAKASH Vs STATE OF U.P. THRU. PRIN. SECY. DEPTT. OF HOME, LKO. AND OTHERS
records.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
records.procedural_role: petitioner (accused in Section 392 IPC robbery investigation)
records.disposition_rationale: High Court bench examined allegations in FIR lodged under Section 392 IPC (chain snatching), noted investigation is underway, held no interference is called for under extraordinary powers under Article 226, and dismissed the writ petition as lacking merit.
records.party_success_rationale: Petitioner was accused seeking to stall police investigation and avoid arrest; State through Learned AGA successfully opposed relief, defended ongoing investigation, and secured dismissal of petition with no stay of arrest granted.

records.case_title: CRL.M.C./3193/2013 of VARUN DUTTA Vs STATE & ANR.
records.procedural_role: petitioner (accused in Crime Branch FIR 129/2013 seeking quashing)
records.disposition_rationale: High Court dismissed Section 482 CrPC quashing petition on substantive merits, holding that petitioner had fled to UK seeking political asylum without court permission, was declared a proclaimed offender, chargesheet was already filed before the trial court, and no case was made out to invoke extraordinary powers under Section 482 CrPC; petition dismissed as devoid of any merit.
records.party_success_rationale: State (through learned APP) and Complainant (Respondent No. 2) vehemently opposed adjournment and quashing, pointed out that chargesheet was already filed and petitioner was a proclaimed offender; State successfully defended the criminal prosecution, and petitioner obtained zero relief.

11.On the basis of forgoing discussions, we are of the considered view thatthe application for leave to appeal lacks merit and deserves to be rejected andthe same is hereby rejected.

12.Since the application for leave to appeal has been rejected, the appealalso does not survive and the same stands dismissed.
records.notes: State Government Appeal under Section 378 CrPC challenging trial court acquittal of accused Rishiram & Ors. High Court affirmed that trial court acquittal was based on proper appreciation and analysis of evidence, held application for leave to appeal lacked merit, rejected leave, and dismissed the appeal. Because the State appeal was dismissed, the accused successfully defended their acquittal under Section 5 Row 122 of guidelines.
records.case_title: A378/37/2015 of STATE OF U.P. Vs RISHIRAM
records.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
records.procedural_role: appellant (State of U.P. appealing against acquittal under Section 378 CrPC)
records.disposition_rationale: State of Uttar Pradesh filed Government Appeal under Section 378 CrPC challenging trial court judgment acquitting accused Rishiram & Ors. High Court reviewed evidence, affirmed that trial court acquittal was based on proper analysis of evidence and was not perverse, rejected leave to appeal on merits, and dismissed the appeal.
records.party_success_rationale: Accused respondents succeeded in defending their acquittal against the State appellate challenge. Under Section 5 Row 122 of guidelines (Criminal Appeal | State/Prosecution | Appeal Dismissed -> accused), successful party is accused.

records.evidence: 12.In view of the above reasoning, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed giving benefit of doubt. Conviction and sentence recorded by the Trial Court are set aside. The appellant shall be released forthwith if not required to be detained in any other criminal case.     13.Trial Court record be sent back forthwith with the copy of the order. A copy of the order be sent to the Superintendent Jail for information.
records.notes: Criminal appeal under Section 374 CrPC by convicted accused Raj Kishore against judgment and order of conviction under Section 376 IPC. High Court held prosecution case suffered from inherent inconsistencies and flaws, prosecutrix testimony unworthy of credit, and medical/FSL evidence absolved accused. Appeal allowed on benefit of doubt, conviction and sentence set aside, and accused ordered released forthwith. Accused appellant completely prevailed against State prosecution.

records.notes: Civil writ petition under Article 226 challenging revocation of customs broker license. Division Bench held that show cause inquiry was not completed within mandatory 90-day timeline and proceedings were invalid as time-barred. High Court set aside the impugned order revoking license and allowed the writ petition with no orders as to costs. Petitioner firm prevailed against Commissioner of Customs.
records.case_title: W.P.(C)/5300/2016 of IMPEXNET LOGISTIC Vs COMMISSIONER OF CUSTOMS(GENERAL)
records.procedural_role: petitioner (customs broker firm challenging license revocation)
records.disposition_rationale: Division Bench held that inquiry report was not submitted within mandatory 90-day period and proceedings were time-barred; set aside Commissioner of Customs order revoking customs broker license and allowed the writ petition.
records.party_success_rationale: Petitioner firm succeeded against the respondent revenue authority, obtaining quashing of the license revocation order and restoration of its license.
